title: Cox and Rodríguez on guidance and control of immigration personnel
shortTitle: Cox and Rodríguez on guidance and control of immigration personnel
summary: Cox and Rodríguez describe how shifting criteria and decisionmakers can alter the implementation of enforcement discretion.
notes: Cox and Rodríguez contrast the Morton memoranda’s broad guidance to enforcement personnel with DACA’s more specific criteria and placement of decisions in USCIS, the benefits-administering component. They attribute the earlier memoranda’s limited effect partly to the enforcement culture and resistance of line agents. Their account explains why leadership might use objective criteria and choose a different component to administer relief. It is an institutional interpretation offered by scholars, and it does not decide the disputed APA classification in Texas.
